arxiv-2205-02462.title: Rate-Splitting Multiple Access for 6G – Part II: Interplay with Integrated Sensing and Communications Thanks: L. Yin, O. Dizdar, and B. Clerckx are with Department of Electrical and Electronic Engineering, Imperial College London, London SW7 2AZ, U.K. (email: {longfei.yin17, o.dizdar, b.clerckx}@imp
arxiv-2205-02462.creator: Longfei Yin, Yijie Mao, Onur Dizdar, and Bruno Clerckx
arxiv-2205-02462.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Longfei Yin, Yijie Mao, Onur Dizdar, and Bruno Clerckx. This letter is the second part of a three-part tutorial focusing on rate-splitting multiple access (RSMA) for 6G. As Part II of the tutorial, this letter addresses the interplay between RSMA and integrated radar sensing and communications (ISAC). In particular, we introduce a general RSMA-assisted ISAC architecture, where the ISAC platform has a dual capability to simultaneously communicate with downlink users and probe detection signals to a moving target.

arxiv-2212-01351.title: A Bayesian Framework for Digital Twin-Based Control, Monitoring, and Data Collection in Wireless Systems C. Ruah and O. Simeone are with King’s Communications, Learning & Information Processing (KCLIP) Lab. The work of O. Simeone was supported by the European Research Council (ERC) under the Europea
arxiv-2212-01351.creator: Clement Ruah, Osvaldo Simeone, and Bashir Al-Hashimi
arxiv-2212-01351.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Clement Ruah, Osvaldo Simeone, and Bashir Al-Hashimi. Commonly adopted in the manufacturing and aerospace sectors, digital twin (DT) platforms are increasingly seen as a promising paradigm to control, monitor, and analyze software-based, “open”, communication systems that are expected to dominate 6G deployments. Notably, DT platforms provide a sandbox in which to test artificial intelligence (AI) solutions for communication systems, potentially reducing the need to collect data and test algorithms in the field, i.e., on the physical twin (PT).

arxiv-2302-13167.title: Transmon probe for quantum characteristics of magnons in antiferromagnets
arxiv-2302-13167.creator: Vahid Azimi-Mousolou, Anders Bergman, Anna Delin, Olle Eriksson, Manuel Pereiro, Danny Thonig, Erik Sjöqvist
arxiv-2302-13167.description: Abstract The detection of magnons and their quantum properties, especially in antiferromagnetic (AFM) materials, is a substantial step to realize many ambitious advances in the study of nanomagnetism and the development of energy efficient quantum technologies. The recent development of hybrid systems based on superconducting circuits provides the possibility of engineering quantum sensors that exploit different degrees of freedom.

arxiv-2308-06488.title: Generating Faithful Text From a Knowledge Graph with Noisy Reference Text
arxiv-2308-06488.creator: Tahsina Hashem, Weiqing Wang, Derry Tanti Wijaya, Mohammed Eunus Ali, Yuan-Fang Li
arxiv-2308-06488.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Tahsina Hashem, Weiqing Wang, Derry Tanti Wijaya, Mohammed Eunus Ali, Yuan-Fang Li. Knowledge Graph (KG)-to-Text generation aims at generating fluent natural-language text that accurately represents the information of a given knowledge graph. While significant progress has been made in this task by exploiting the power of pre-trained language models (PLMs) with appropriate graph structure-aware modules, existing models still fall short of generating faithful text, especially when the ground-truth natural-language text contains additional information that is not present in the graph.

arxiv-2309-13726.title: A compact 20-pass thin-disk multipass amplifier stable against thermal lensing effects and delivering 330 mJ pulses with 𝐌 𝟐 < 1.17 \bf{M^{2}<1.17} Journal: oe Publication type: Research Article
arxiv-2309-13726.creator: Manuel Zeyen, 1 Lukas Affolter, 1 Marwan Abdou Ahmed, 2 Thomas Graf, 2 Oguzhan Kara, 1 Klaus Kirch, 1,3 Miroslaw Marszalek, 1 François Nez, 4 Ahmed Ouf, 5 Randolf Pohl, 5,6 Siddharth Rajamohanan, 5 Pauline Yzombard, 4 Karsten Schuhmann 1 and Aldo Antognini 1,3,*
arxiv-2309-13726.description: Abstract We report on an Yb:YAG thin-disk multipass amplifier delivering 50 ns long pulses at a central wavelength of 1030 nm with an energy of 330 mJ at a repetition rate of 100 Hz. The beam quality factor at the maximum energy was measured to be M 2 = 1.17 \text{M}^{2}=1.17 .

arxiv-2404-05158.title: Quantum and Classical Two-photon Interference of Single Photons with Ultralong Coherence Time
arxiv-2404-05158.creator: Manman Wang, Yanfeng Li, Hanqing Liu, Haiqiao Ni, Zhichuan Niu, Xiaogang Wei, Renfu Yang, Chengyong Hu
arxiv-2404-05158.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Manman Wang, Yanfeng Li, Hanqing Liu, Haiqiao Ni, Zhichuan Niu, Xiaogang Wei, Renfu Yang, Chengyong Hu. Two-photon interference (TPI) is a fundamental phenomenon in quantum optics and plays a crucial role in quantum information science and technology. TPI is commonly considered as quantum interference with an upper bound of 100 % 100\% for both the TPI visibility and the beat visibility in contrast to its classical counterpart with a maximum visibility of 50 % 50\% . However, this is not always the case.

arxiv-2408-11924.title: On reduced basis methods for eigenvalue problems, and on its coupling with perturbation theory
arxiv-2408-11924.creator: Louis Garrigue, Benjamin Stamm
arxiv-2408-11924.description: Abstract . In this article, we study eigenvalue problems associated to self-adjoint operators and their approximation obtained by subspace projection, as used in the reduced basis method for instance. We provide error bounds between the exact eigenmodes and the approximated ones and also consider degenerate cases in the analysis.

arxiv-2411-04832.title: Plasticity Loss in Deep Reinforcement Learning: A Survey
arxiv-2411-04832.creator: Timo Klein, Christoph Luther, Manus McAuliffe, Lukas Miklautz, Claudia Plant, Sebastian Tschiatschek
arxiv-2411-04832.description: Abstract . Plasticity refers to a network’s ability to adapt to changing data distributions, which is crucial for the successful training of deep reinforcement learning agents. Loss of plasticity causes performance plateaus and contributes to scaling failures, overestimation bias, and insufficient exploration.

arxiv-2502-14177.title: InstaSHAP: Interpretable Additive Models Explain Shapley Values Instantly
arxiv-2502-14177.creator: James Enouen, Yan Liu
arxiv-2502-14177.description: Abstract In recent years, the Shapley value and SHAP explanations have emerged as one of the most dominant paradigms for providing post-hoc explanations of black-box models. Despite their well-founded theoretical properties, many recent works have focused on the limitations in both their computational efficiency and their representation power.

arxiv-2511-11714.title: Federated Learning for Pediatric Pneumonia Detection: Enabling Collaborative Diagnosis Without Sharing Patient Data
arxiv-2511-11714.creator: Sherpa.ai
arxiv-2511-11714.description: Abstract Early and accurate pneumonia detection from chest X-rays (CXRs) is clinically critical to expedite treatment and isolation, reduce complications, and curb unnecessary antibiotic use. Although artificial intelligence (AI) substantially improves CXR-based detection, development is hindered by globally distributed data, high inter-hospital variability, and strict privacy regulations (e.g., HIPAA, GDPR) that make centralization impractical.

plos-pone-0007981.description: PLOS ONE research article. Plant viruses such as Cowpea mosaic virus (CPMV) are increasingly being developed for applications in nanobiotechnology including vaccine development because of their potential for producing large quantities of antigenic material in plant hosts. pmc-10738371.title: LIFELONG LEARNING AND SELF-EFFICACY OF PHYSICAL ACTIVITY ENGAGEMENT IN SEDENTARY OLDER ADULTS: A QUALITATIVE STUDY
pmc-10738371.creator: Claire Wang, Mengchi Li, Jing Huang, Yeabsira Tufa, Junxin LI
pmc-10738371.description: Societal-level norms play an essential role in later-life sentiments surrounding learning. While there is a wealth of literature on the benefits of learning new skills in improving health and physical capacity, there is a gap in how learning perceptions can influence willingness to learn in contemplation, action, and outcome.

pmc-10783654.title: Plasmodium falciparum exploits CD44 as a coreceptor for erythrocyte invasion
pmc-10783654.creator: Barbara Baro, Chi Yong Kim, Carrie Lin, Angel K. Kongsomboonvech, Marilou Tetard, Nana Ansuah Peterson, Nichole D. Salinas, Niraj H. Tolia, Elizabeth S. Egan

Introduction Malaria due to the apicomplexan parasite Plasmodium falciparum is a leading cause of morbidity and mortality in the developing world.

pmc-11623074.title: Facial expression morphing: enhancing visual fidelity and preserving facial details in CycleGAN-based expression synthesis
pmc-11623074.creator: Chayanon Sub-r-pa, Rung-Ching Chen, Ming-Zhong Fan
pmc-11623074.description: Recent advancements in facial expression synthesis using deep learning, particularly with Cycle-Consistent Adversarial Networks (CycleGAN), have led to impressive results. However, a critical challenge persists: the generated expressions often lack the sharpness and fine details of the original face, such as freckles, moles, or birthmarks.

pmc-11624408.title: Ventricular arrhythmias after atrial fibrillation electrical cardioversion: A multicenter study
pmc-11624408.creator: Oholi Tovia-Brodie, Yoav Michowitz, Feras Bayya, Stepan Havranek, Milan Dusik, Luigi Rivetti, Roberto Mantovan, Avi Sabbag, Eyas Massalha, Pietro Enea Lazzerini, Iacopo Bertolozzi, Giovanni Malanchini, Christoffer Tobias Witt, Óscar Cano, Ziv Dadon, Michael Ilan, Pieter G. Postema, Michael Glikson,
pmc-11624408.description: BackgroundVentricular arrhythmias (VAs) after atrial fibrillation (AF) electrical cardioversion (ECV) have been reported.ObjectiveWe sought to assess incidence, timing, and clinical characteristics of patients with post-AF ECV-related VAs.MethodsMulticenter observational retrospective study including 13 centers, incorporating patients with VAs or sudden cardiac death within 10 days of ECV. The total number of ECVs performed during the collecting period was provided.

pmc-11663971.title: A comprehensive dataset of near infrared spectroscopy measurements to predict nitrogen and carbon contents in a wide range of tissues from Brassica napus plants grown under contrasted environments
pmc-11663971.creator: Sophie Rolland, Françoise Leprince, Solenn Guichard, Françoise Le Cahérec, Anne Laperche, Nathalie Nesi
pmc-11663971.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Winter oilseed rape (WOSR, Brassica napus L.) is the third largest oil crop worldwide that also provides a source of high quality plant-based proteins. Nitrogen (N) and carbon (C) play a key role in plant growth. Determination of N and C contents of plant tissues throughout the growth cycle is crucial in assessing plant nutritional status and allowing precise input management.

pmc-11671309.title: Differential Trends in Health Care Utilization and Spending Among Asian American and Pacific Islander Medicare Beneficiaries before and During the COVID-19 Pandemic
pmc-11671309.creator: Taylor Melanson, Tanvi Rao, Aditi Pathak, Mike Liu, Tracy Haidar, Rouguia Barry
pmc-11671309.description: Introduction:The COVID-19 pandemic placed unprecedented strains on the U.S. health care system, contributing to significant disruptions of care. COVID-19 was also associated with an increase in negative sentiment toward and hate crimes targeting Asian Americans and Pacific Islanders (AAPI) individuals.

pmc-11689452.title: EDUCATION ON COMMUNICATION WHILE WEARING FACEMASKS USEFUL DESPITE THE END OF COVID-19 EMERGENCY
pmc-11689452.creator: Clarissa Shaw, Kristine Williams, Carissa Coleman, Lynn Nakad
pmc-11689452.description: Communication with nursing home residents by formal caregivers is complicated with the use of facemasks. Yet facemask use is necessary to limit the spread of disease during surges of communicable respiratory illnesses. The purpose of this study was to develop and pilot test a web-based educational module to promote successful communication with nursing home residents while wearing facemasks.

pmc-12370045.title: Research on the impact path of virtual streamers characteristics on agricultural product consumers’ purchase intention
pmc-12370045.creator: Lin Jiang, Min Li, Vincenzo Auriemma, Vincenzo Auriemma, Vincenzo Auriemma
pmc-12370045.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Live-streaming e-commerce for agricultural product has become a new exploration in rural revitalization and digital commerce in China, with AI-driven virtual streamers emerging as a new trend in this field. Focusing on the context of virtual streamers marketing, this study constructs a relationship model between virtual streamers characteristics and consumers’ purchase intention for agricultural products, using human-machine trust as a moderating variable and communication presence and emotional presence as mediating variables.

pmc-12447561.title: Head and Neck Cancer in Fanconi Anemia: Clinical Challenges and Molecular Insights into a DNA Repair Disorder
pmc-12447561.creator: Juhye Choi, Moonjung Jung, Yanhong Liu
pmc-12447561.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Simple SummaryFanconi anemia is an inherited bone marrow failure syndrome with an increased incidence of cancers due to DNA repair deficiency. Head and neck cancer is the most common solid cancer type in patients with Fanconi anemia. In this review article, we summarize clinical manifestations and discuss recent discoveries in the molecular pathogenesis of tumor formation and progression in DNA repair disorder, Fanconi anemia.

pmc-12561012.title: Living with Risk, Aging with Uncertainty: A Narrative Review of Health and Genetic Vulnerability in Huntington’s Disease
pmc-12561012.creator: Adriana V Muñoz-Ortega, David Conde Caballero, Lorenzo Mariano Juárez, Marie-Lise Maddelein
pmc-12561012.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background/Objectives: Huntington’s disease (HD) is an autosomal dominant, neurodegenerative disorder that, because of the availability of presymptomatic genetic testing, places at-risk individuals in an anticipatory situation of great emotional, ethical, and social complexity. This review synthesizes the subjective experiences and coping strategies of individuals aware of their genetic risk before clinical diagnosis, emphasizing the importance of patient and family narratives as critical sources of evidence for enhancing care protocols. Methods: This work is a narrative review supported by a systematic literature search.

pmc-12581111.title: Optimized Kappa‐Index Test Protocol to Detect Intrathecal Immunoglobulin Synthesis in Multiple Sclerosis
pmc-12581111.creator: Joel Björklund, Outi Itkonen, Pasi Nokelainen, Mika Siuko, Emilia Österlund‐Tauriala, Pentti J Tienari, Mikko Anttonen
pmc-12581111.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). BackgroundKappa free light chain (KFLC)‐based Kappa‐index (K‐index) can substitute oligoclonal banding (OCB) to detect intrathecal immunoglobulin synthesis. Cutoffs for positive results vary; therefore, further comparison of different approaches is necessary to optimize K‐index for diagnostic utilization.MethodsWe analyzed 432 paired CSF/serum samples and selected 77 OCB‐positive patients with multiple sclerosis (MS), clinically isolated syndrome (CIS) that did not progress to MS in > 10 years, and other neuroinflammatory diseases (non‐MS).

pmc-12679328.title: Instant Artificial Bone Preparation From Silicone and Resin: Need of the Hour
pmc-12679328.creator: Jakkula Akhil, Nutan Nalini Bage, Rema Devi
pmc-12679328.description: Osteology is an important foundation for medical students to understand the framework of the human body. In the recent past, there has been a scarcity of natural resources of human bones, while the number of students and colleges has been drastically increasing.

pmc-13171526.title: Prediction of infection in the emergency department—a machine learning model
pmc-13171526.creator: Sara N. Søgaard, Helene Skjøt-Arkil, Christian Backer Mogensen, Flemming Schønning Rosenvinge, Thomas Kronborg
pmc-13171526.description: BackgroundThe integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into emergency medicine holds promise for enhancing early diagnosis and clinical decision-making. Traditional diagnostic approaches often rely on physician judgment or early warning scores that may delay identification of infections, especially when these tools prioritize outcomes such as mortality or ICU admission over early infection detection.

pmc-13232922.title: The Evolving Burden of Stroke in China’s 832 Poverty-Alleviated Counties (2019-2024): Nationwide Spatiotemporal Analysis
pmc-13232922.creator: Mengdi Chen, Dong Xia, Wenping Li, Jie Wang, Zhiyu Lv, Jiapeng Chen, Lulu Zhang
pmc-13232922.description: BackgroundStroke remains a leading cause of death and disability in China. Despite the nationwide poverty alleviation being achieved by 2020, residents of poverty-alleviated counties continue to experience poorer health outcomes. There is a critical knowledge gap regarding the evolving spatiotemporal patterns of stroke burden in this large postpoverty population.

pmc-13250957.title: Survey Showed That Limiting Daily Screen Time Could Help to Avoid Mental Health Issues in Children Aged 8–17Years
pmc-13250957.creator: Anders Carlander, Sophie Cassel, Malin J‐son Höök, Oskar Lundgren, Ann‐Sophie Lindqvist Bagge, Marie Löf
pmc-13250957.description: AimThis study tested the associations between screen time and anxiety and depression, while accounting for physical activity, sleep and socioeconomic background.MethodsWe analysed repeated cross‐sectional survey data from the Swedish population‐based Generation Pep Study, which was collected in 2021–2022 and comprised children aged 8–17 years.

pmc-13518088.creator: Brian Rayner, Kenneth W Mahaffey, Johannes F E Mann, Richard E Pratley, Peter Rossing, Nicolas Belmar, Heidrun Bosch-Traberg, Ole Kleist Jeppesen, Minh Chau Tran, Gil Chernin, Katherine R Tuttle

pmc-13560876.title: Bottom-up design of Ca2+ channels from defined selectivity filter geometry
pmc-13560876.creator: Yulai Liu, Connor Weidle, Ljubica Mihaljević, Joseph L. Watson, Zhe Li, Le Tracy Yu, Sagardip Majumder, Andrew J. Borst, Kenneth D. Carr, Ryan D. Kibler, Tamer M. Gamal El-Din, William A. Catterall, David Baker
pmc-13560876.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Native ion channels play key roles in biological systems, and engineered versions are widely used as chemogenetic tools and in sensing devices1,2. Protein design has been harnessed to generate pore-containing transmembrane proteins, but the design of selectivity filters with precise arrangements of amino acid sidechains specific for a target ion, a crucial feature of native ion channels3, has been constrained by the lack of methods to place the metal-coordinating residues with atomic-level precision.
